parameters.name: Frequency command
parameters.description: This parameter sets the frequency that the inverter is commanded to output. During Stop: Frequency Command. During Run: Output Frequency. During Multi-step operation: Multi-step frequency 0. It cannot be set greater than F21- [Max frequency].

parameters.name: Accel time
parameters.description: During Multi-Accel/Decel operation, this parameter serves as Accel/Decel time 0.

parameters.name: Decel time
parameters.description: During Multi-Accel/Decel operation, this parameter serves as Accel/Decel time 0.

parameters.name: Drive mode
parameters.description: Chapter 7.3 (printed 7-8, 7-9): drv 0: acceleration starts with the Run key and the motor decelerates to stop with STOP/RST (direction via drC). drv 1: FX/RX terminals (set I17=0, I18=1 so P1 = FX forward run, P2 = RX reverse run); the motor stops when FX and RX are ON/OFF at the same time. drv 2: FX gives the run command, RX selects direction (reverse when ON). drv 3: operation via RS485 (set I59, I60, I61).
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Footnote 1): Option 4 "This function can be available with iG5A Communication Option Module."

options.label: Run/Stop via Run/Stop key on the keypad
Terminal operation (FX: Motor forward run, RX: Motor reverse run)
Terminal operation (FX: Run/Stop enable, RX: Reverse rotation select)

parameters.name: Frequency setting method
parameters.description: Chapter 7.1 (printed 7-1 to 7-6): Frq 0: keypad setting 1 (set the value in 0.00 and press Ent). Frq 1: keypad setting 2 (Up/Down keys act as a potentiometer). Frq 2: -10~+10V on V1-CM (I2~I5, I6~I10). Frq 3: 0~10V or potentiometer on VR, V1, CM (I6~I10). Frq 4: 0~20mA on I-CM (I11~I15). Frq 5/6: V1 + I override (main/auxiliary speed). Frq 7: RS485 (I59~I61). Frq 8: Digital Volume (up-down). Frequency must be less than F21.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Footnote 1): Option 9 "This function can be available with iG5A Communication Option Module."

options.label: Analog: Terminal V1 setting 1 + Terminal I
Analog: Terminal V1 setting 2 + Terminal I

parameters.name: Multi-Step freq. 1
parameters.description: Sets Multi-Step frequency 1 during Multi-step operation.

parameters.name: Multi-Step freq. 2
parameters.description: Sets Multi-Step frequency 2 during Multi-step operation.

parameters.name: Multi-Step freq. 3
parameters.description: Sets Multi-Step frequency 3 during Multi-step operation.

parameters.name: Output current
parameters.description: Displays the output current to the motor.

parameters.name: Motor RPM
parameters.description: Displays the number of Motor RPM.

parameters.name: Inverter DC link voltage
parameters.description: Displays DC link voltage inside the inverter.

parameters.name: User display select
parameters.description: This parameter displays the item selected at H73- [Monitoring item select].

parameters.name: Fault Display
parameters.description: Displays the types of faults, frequency and operating status at the time of the fault

parameters.name: Direction of motor rotation select
parameters.description: Sets the direction of motor rotation when drv - [Drive mode] is set to either 0 or 1. Chapter 7.3 (printed 7-8): Selects the rotation direction when the operating command is issued via keypad (F forward, r reverse).
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: Yes. Range printed as "F, r".
parameters.evidence_quote: drC A10D [Direction of motor rotation select]

parameters.name: Drive mode 2
parameters.description: Chapter 8.16 (printed 8-22): Second drive mode, used when a multi-function input set to 22 (2nd Source) is ON; otherwise drv is used. Useful to leave communication drive and operate locally. Check Drive mode 2 before turning the 2nd-source terminal ON.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Footnote 3): Option 4 "This function can be available with iG5A Communication Option Module."

options.label: Run/Stop via Run/Stop key on the keypad
Terminal operation (FX: Motor forward run, RX: Motor reverse run)
Terminal operation (FX: Run/Stop enable, RX: Reverse rotation select)

parameters.name: Frequency setting method 2
parameters.description: Chapter 8.16 (printed 8-22, 8-23): Second frequency setting method, used when the 2nd Source input is ON (same options as Frq); frequency command and drive command both switch to the 2nd mode.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Only displayed when one of the Multi-function input terminals 1-8 [I17~I24] is set to "22". Footnote 1): Option 9 "This function can be available with iG5A Communication Option Module."

options.label: Analog: Terminal V1 setting 1 + Terminal I
Analog: Terminal V1 setting 2 + Terminal I

parameters.name: PID control standard value setting
parameters.description: If H58 is 0, it is expressed as a [Hz] unit. If H58 is 1, it is expressed as a [%] unit. In [Hz] unit, you can't set Max. frequency more than (F21). In [%] unit, 100% means Max. frequency.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes. Range printed as "0~400 [Hz] or 0~100 [%]". It is indicated when H49 (PID control selection) is 1.
parameters.evidence_quote: rEF 2) A110 PID control standard value setting

parameters.name: PID control feedback amount
parameters.description: It indicates a feedback amount in PID control. If H58 is 0, it is expressed as a [Hz] unit. If H58 is 1, it is expressed as a [%] unit.
parameters.setting_conditions: It is indicated when H49 (PID control selection) is 1.
parameters.evidence_quote: Fbk 2) A111 PID control feedback amount It indicates a feedback amount in PID

parameters.name: Jump code
parameters.description: Sets the parameter code number to jump.

parameters.name: Forward/Reverse run disable
parameters.description: Chapter 7.3 (printed 7-10): FX/RX run disable: 0 forward and reverse run enabled, 1 forward run disabled, 2 reverse run disabled.

parameters.name: Accel pattern
parameters.description: Chapter 7.4 (printed 7-15): Accel pattern: Linear is a general pattern for constant torque applications; S-curve gives smooth acceleration (actual Accel time becomes longer than set). Shape set by H17/H18.

parameters.name: Decel pattern
parameters.description: Decel pattern selection (range, options, default and Adj. cells are shared with F2 in the table). Chapter 7.4 (printed 7-15): Decel pattern: Linear or S-curve (actual Decel time becomes longer than set). Shape set by H17/H18.

parameters.name: Stop mode select
parameters.description: Chapter 7.6 (printed 7-20): 0 motor decelerates to 0 Hz and stops during the set time; 1 DC brake to stop (F8-F11); 2 free run stop (output frequency and voltage cut off when operating command is OFF); 3 Power Braking stop (see 8.17).

parameters.name: DC Brake start frequency
parameters.description: This parameter sets DC brake start frequency. It cannot be set below F23 - [Start frequency]. Chapter 8.1 (printed 8-1): Frequency at which the DC brake becomes active during DC-brake stop (F4 = 1).
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Only displayed when F 4 is set to 1 (DC brake to stop).

parameters.name: DC Brake wait time
parameters.description: When DC brake frequency is reached, the inverter holds the output for the setting time before starting DC brake. Chapter 8.1 (printed 8-1): Inverter output holds for this time after F8 before applying F10; a larger value helps prevent over current trip with large load inertia or high F8.
parameters.evidence_quote: 5.00 X F 9 A209 [DC Brake wait time]

parameters.name: DC Brake voltage
parameters.description: This parameter sets the amount of DC voltage applied to a motor. It is set in percent of H33 - [Motor rated current]. Chapter 8.1 (printed 8-1): Setting F10 or F11 to 0 disables DC brake. Excessive DC brake voltage or time may overheat and damage the motor.

parameters.name: DC Brake time
parameters.description: This parameter sets the time taken to apply DC current to a motor while motor is at a stop.

parameters.name: DC Brake start voltage
parameters.description: This parameter sets the amount of DC voltage before a motor starts to run. It is set in percent of H33 - [Motor rated current]. Chapter 8.1 (printed 8-2): Starting DC brake: voltage as percent of H33 applied before the motor starts; setting F12 or F13 to 0 disables starting DC brake. Also used for DC brake during stop (multi-function input = 11).

parameters.name: DC Brake start time
parameters.description: DC voltage is applied to the motor for DC Brake start time before motor accelerates.

parameters.name: Time for magnetizing a motor
parameters.description: This parameter applies the current to a motor for the set time before motor accelerates during Sensorless vector control. Chapter 8.9 (printed 8-14): Pre-excites the motor for the set time before acceleration in sensorless vector control; the pre-excitation current is set in H34.
parameters.evidence_quote: F14 A20E [Time for magneti zing a

parameters.name: Jog frequency
parameters.description: This parameter sets the frequency for Jog operation. It cannot be set above F21 - [Max frequency]. Chapter 8.2 (printed 8-3): Jog frequency, settable within F21 and F23. Jog operation overrides all other operations except Dwell; selected by a multi-function input set to 4 (Jog), 26 (JOG-FX) or 27 (JOG-RX).

parameters.name: Max frequency
parameters.description: This parameter sets the highest frequency the inverter can output. It is frequency reference for Accel/Decel (See H70). Caution: Any frequency cannot be set above Max frequency except Base frequency. Chapter 7.7 (printed 7-21): Frequency highest limit; no frequency can be set above Max frequency except F22 Base frequency. It is also the reference for Accel/Decel time when H70 = 0.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. If H40 is set to 3 (Sensorless vector), Max. frequency is settable up to 300Hz.

parameters.name: Base frequency
parameters.description: The inverter outputs its rated voltage to the motor at this frequency (see motor nameplate). Chapter 7.5 (printed 7-17): Inverter outputs its rated voltage at this frequency; enter the motor nameplate frequency.

parameters.name: Start frequency
parameters.description: The inverter starts to output its voltage at this frequency. It is the frequency low limit. Chapter 7.7 (printed 7-21): Frequency lowest limit; if a frequency is set lower than this, 0.00 is automatically set.

parameters.name: Frequency high/low limit select
parameters.description: This parameter sets high and low limit of run frequency. Chapter 7.7 (printed 7-21): Set to 1 to limit the active run frequency within F25 and F26; also valid for analog (voltage/current) and keypad setting.

parameters.name: Frequency high limit
parameters.description: This parameter sets high limit of the run frequency. It cannot be set above F21 - [Max frequency].
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Only displayed when F24 (Frequency high/low limit select) is set to 1.

parameters.name: Frequency low limit
parameters.description: This parameter sets low limit of the run frequency. It cannot be set above F25 - [Frequency high limit] and below F23 - [Start frequency].

parameters.name: Torque Boost select
parameters.description: Chapter 7.5 (printed 7-19): 0 Manual torque boost (values in F28, F29); 1 Auto torque boost (the inverter calculates the boost from motor parameters; set H34 and H42 correctly first). Too high a manual boost may overheat the motor.
parameters.evidence_quote: 0.50 X 0 Manual torque boost F27 A21B [Torque Boost select]

parameters.name: Torque boost in forward direction
parameters.description: This parameter sets the amount of torque boost applied to a motor during forward run. It is set in percent of Max output voltage.
parameters.evidence_quote: F28 A21C [Torque boost in forward direction]

parameters.name: Torque boost in reverse direction
parameters.description: This parameter sets the amount of torque boost applied to a motor during reverse run. It is set as a percent of Max output voltage
parameters.evidence_quote: F29 A21D [Torque boost in reverse direction]

parameters.name: V/F pattern
parameters.description: Chapter 7.5 (printed 7-17, 7-18): 0 Linear: constant V/F ratio from F23 to F22, for constant torque; 1 Square: squared V/F ratio, for fans and pumps; 2 User V/F: 4-point pattern F31-F38 (F28/F29 torque boost are deactivated).

parameters.name: User V/F frequency 1
parameters.description: It is used only when V/F pattern is set to 2(User V/F). It cannot be set above F21 - [Max frequency]. The value of voltage is set in percent of H70 - [Motor rated voltage]. The values of the lower-numbered parameters cannot be set above those of higher-numbered.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Set F30 to 2(User V/F) to display this parameter.

parameters.name: Output voltage adjustment
parameters.description: This parameter adjusts the amount of output voltage. The set value is the percentage of input voltage. Chapter 7.5 (printed 7-18): Adjusts the inverter output voltage; useful for motors with rated voltage lower than the input voltage.

parameters.name: Energy-saving level
parameters.description: This parameter decreases output voltage according to load status. Chapter 8.10 (printed 8-15): Percent of max output voltage that is reduced at light/no load; for fan or pump applications it can reduce energy consumption.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

parameters.name: Electronic thermal select
parameters.description: This parameter is activated when the motor is overheated (time-inverse). Chapter 10.1 (printed 10-1): Set to 1 to enable electronic thermal protection; when current above F51 flows the output is turned off after the preset time.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

parameters.name: Electronic thermal level for 1 minute
parameters.description: This parameter sets max current capable of flowing to the motor continuously for 1 minute. The set value is the percentage of H33 - [Motor rated current]. It cannot be set below F52 - [Electronic thermal level for continuous].
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes. Set F50 to 1 to display this parameter.

parameters.name: Electronic thermal level for continuous
parameters.description: This parameter sets the amount of current to keep the motor running continuously. It cannot be set higher than F51 - [Electronic thermal level for 1 minute].
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes
parameters.evidence_quote: F52 A234 [Electronic thermal level for continuous]

parameters.name: Motor cooling method
parameters.description: Chapter 10.1 (printed 10-1): Cooling effect of a standard motor decreases at low speed; a special motor uses a separately powered cooling fan.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

options.label: Standard motor having cooling fan directly connected to the shaft.
A motor using a separate motor to power a cooling fan.

parameters.name: Overload warning level
parameters.description: This parameter sets the amount of current to issue an alarm signal at a relay or multi-function output terminal (see I54, I55). The set value is the percentage of H33- [Motor rated current]. Chapter 10.2 (printed 10-2): Overload warning: percent of motor rated current; the warning is output at MO/3ABC when set to 5 {OLt} in I54/I55 after F55.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

parameters.name: Overload warning time
parameters.description: This parameter issues an alarm signal when the current greater than F54- [Overload warning level] flows to the motor for F55- [Overload warning time].
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

parameters.name: Overload trip select
parameters.description: This parameter turns off the inverter output when motor is overloaded. Chapter 10.2 (printed 10-3): Overload trip: set to 1 to turn off the output when current above F57 flows for F58.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

parameters.name: Overload trip level
parameters.description: This parameter sets the amount of overload current. The value is the percentage of H33- [Motor rated current].
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

parameters.name: Overload trip time
parameters.description: This parameter turns off the inverter output when the F57- [Overload trip level] of current flows to the motor for F58- [Overload trip time].
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

parameters.name: Stall prevention select
parameters.description: This parameter stops accelerating during acceleration, decelerating during constant speed run and stops decelerating during decal. Selection by bits: Bit 2 = During Decel., Bit 1 = During constant run, Bit 0 = During Accel. (values 0-7; the check marks of the bit table are not in the text layer) Chapter 10.3 (printed 10-3, 10-4): Stall prevention by bits (accel / constant speed / decel). Accel: motor starts to decelerate when current above F60 flows; constant run: motor decelerates; decel: deceleration stops when DC link voltage rises above a level. Accel/Decel time may become longer than set. Used with F4 = 3 Power Braking (8.17).

parameters.name: Stall prevention level
parameters.description: This parameter sets the amount of current to activate stall prevention function during Accel, Constant or Decel run. The set value is the percentage of the H33- [Motor rated current].

parameters.name: When Stall prevention during decal., voltage limit select
parameters.description: In Stall prevention run during deceleration, if you want to limit output voltage, select 1
parameters.setting_conditions: It is indicated when setting bit 2 of F59 as 1

parameters.name: Save up/down frequency select
parameters.description: This parameter decides whether to save the specified frequency during up/down operation. When 1 is selected, the up/down frequency is saved in F64. Chapter 8.3 (printed 8-4): If 1, the frequency before the inverter stops or decelerates is saved in F64 (up-down save function); can be initialized with a multi-function input set to 25.

parameters.name: Save up/down frequency
parameters.description: If 'Save up/down frequency' is selected at F63, this parameter saves the frequency before the inverter stops or decelerated.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Set F63 to 1 to display this parameter.

parameters.name: Up-down mode select
parameters.description: We can select up-down mode among three thing Chapter 8.3 (printed 8-5, 8-6): 0: frequency increases/decreases toward Max/Min frequency while UP/DOWN is held; 1: changes by step frequency F66 on each edge; 2: combination (a held input for 3 s acts like mode 0).

options.label: Increases goal frequency as a standard of Max. frequency/Min. frequency
Increases as many as step freq. according to edge input.

parameters.name: Up-down step frequency
parameters.description: In case of choosing F65 as a 1 or 2, it means increase or decrease of frequency according to up-down input

parameters.name: Draw run mode select
parameters.description: Chapter 8.20 (printed 8-26, 8-27): DRAW drive is open-loop tension control using the speed difference of the motor under the main frequency command. Set the command frequency in FRQ/FRQ2 and the rest by F70/F71.

options.label: Inverter doesn't run as a draw mode

parameters.name: Draw rate
parameters.description: Sets rate of draw
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: printed as '0' in the text layer (O/X glyph); read as Yes

parameters.name: Jump code
parameters.description: Sets the code number to jump.

parameters.name: Fault history 1
parameters.description: Stores information on the types of faults, the frequency, the current and the Accel/Decel condition at the time of fault. The latest fault is automatically stored in the H 1- [Fault history 1].

parameters.name: Reset fault history
parameters.description: Clears the fault history saved in H 1-5.

parameters.name: Dwell frequency
parameters.description: When run frequency is issued, motor starts to accelerate after dwell frequency is applied to the motor during H8- [Dwell time]. [Dwell frequency] can be set within the range of F21- [Max frequency] and F23- [Start frequency]. Chapter 8.5 (printed 8-7): Motor accelerates after running at the dwell frequency for the dwell time H8; mainly used to release a mechanical brake in elevators/hoisting.

parameters.name: Dwell time
parameters.description: Sets the time for dwell operation.

parameters.name: Skip frequency select
parameters.description: Sets the frequency range to skip to prevent undesirable resonance and vibration on the structure of the machine.

parameters.name: Skip frequency low limit 1
parameters.description: Run frequency cannot be set within the range of H11 thru H16. The frequency values of the low numbered parameters cannot be set above those of the high numbered ones. Settable within the range of F21 and F23.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. only displayed when H10 is set to 1.

parameters.name: S-Curve accel/decel start side
parameters.description: Set the speed reference value to form a curve at the start during accel/decel. If it is set higher, linear zone gets smaller. Chapter 7.4 (printed 7-15): Starting ratio between S-curve and Linear in 1/2 of the Accel/Decel reference frequency.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. H17, H18 are used when F2, F3 are set to 1 (S-curve).

parameters.name: S-Curve accel/decel end side
parameters.description: Set the speed reference value to form a curve at the end during accel/decel. If it is set higher, linear zone gets smaller. Chapter 7.4 (printed 7-15): Ending ratio between S-curve and Linear in 1/2 of the Accel/Decel reference frequency.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. H17, H18 are used when F2, F3 are set to 1 (S-curve).

parameters.name: Input/output phase loss protection select
parameters.description: Chapter 10.4 (printed 10-5): Output phase loss: output shut off if more than one of U, V, W is lost; input phase loss: blocked if more than one of R, S, T is lost (or when the DC link capacitor needs replacing). Set H33 correctly or the protection may not activate.
parameters.evidence_quote: H19 A313 [Input/output phase loss protection select] 2 Input

parameters.name: Power On Start select
parameters.description: This parameter is activated when drv is set to 1 or 2 (Run/Stop via Control terminal). Motor starts acceleration after AC power is applied while FX or RX terminal is ON. Chapter 7.3 (printed 7-11): Set to 1: motor starts suddenly when AC power is applied with drv = 1/2 and FX/RX ON; inactive for drv 0 or 3. Take care of the hazard.

parameters.name: Restart after fault reset selection
parameters.description: This parameter is activated when drv is set to 1 or 2 (Run/Stop via Control terminal). Motor accelerates after the fault condition is reset while the FX or RX terminal is ON. Chapter 7.3 (printed 7-11): Set to 1: motor starts acceleration when a fault is reset with FX/RX ON; inactive for drv 0 or 3. Take care of the hazard.
parameters.evidence_quote: H21 A315 [Restart after fault reset selection]

parameters.name: Speed Search Select
parameters.description: This parameter is active to prevent any possible fault when the inverter outputs its voltage to the running motor. Selection by bits (Bit 0: 4. Normal accel., Bit 1: 3. Operation after fault, Bit 2: 2. Restart after instant power failure, Bit 3: 1. H20-[Power On start]); values 0-15 (the check marks of the bit table are not in the text layer). Normal acceleration has first priority. Even though #4 is selected along with other bits, Inverter performs Speed search #4. Chapter 8.11 (printed 8-16): Speed search bits: bit0 during acceleration, bit1 restart after fault reset (H21), bit2 restart after instant power failure, bit3 Power ON start (H20). The inverter estimates rpm from the output current. I54/I55 = 15 outputs the speed-search signal.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: Yes. Footnote 1): Normal acceleration has first priority. Even though #4 is selected along with other bits, Inverter performs Speed search #4. The bit table continues on page 55 (values 5-15).

parameters.name: Current level during Speed search
parameters.description: This parameter limits the amount of current during speed search. The set value is the percentage of the H33- [Motor rated current].

parameters.name: P gain during Speed search
parameters.description: It is the Proportional gain used for Speed Search PI controller.
parameters.evidence_quote: H24 A318 [P gain during Speed search]

parameters.name: I gain during speed search
parameters.description: It is the Integral gain used for Speed search PI controller.
parameters.evidence_quote: H25 A319 [I gain during speed search]

parameters.name: Number of Auto Restart try
parameters.description: This parameter sets the number of restart tries after a fault occurs. Auto Restart is deactivated if the fault outnumbers the restart tries. This function is active when [drv] is set to 1 or 2 {Run/Stop via control terminal}. Deactivated during active protection function (OHT, LVT, EXT, HWT etc.). Chapter 8.12 (printed 8-18): Auto restart count is reduced by 1 each restart and restored if no trip occurs for 30 s; restart after H27 via speed search; deactivated after Lvt, EST, Oht or HWt.
parameters.evidence_quote: H26 A31A [Number of Auto Restart try]

parameters.name: Auto Restart time
parameters.description: This parameter sets the time between restart tries.

parameters.name: Motor type select
parameters.description: Motor type (capacity) selection; settable values run from 0.2 (0.2kW) to 22.0 (22.0kW). Chapter 8.6 (printed 8-8): Sets the motor capacity connected to the inverter output.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. H30 is preset based on inverter rating.

parameters.name: Number of motor poles
parameters.description: This setting is displayed via rPM in drive group.

parameters.name: Rated slip frequency
parameters.description: Rated slip frequency fs = fr - (rpm x P / 120), where fs = Rated slip frequency, fr = Rated frequency, rpm = Motor nameplate RPM, P = Number of Motor poles Chapter 8.6 (printed 8-8): Rated slip frequency fs = fr - (rpm x P / 120); e.g. 60 Hz, 1740 rpm, 4 poles gives 2 Hz.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. H32 ~ H36 factory default values are set based on OTIS-LG motor.

parameters.name: Motor rated current
parameters.description: Enter motor rated current on the nameplate.

parameters.name: No Load Motor Current
parameters.description: Enter the current value detected when the motor is rotating in rated rpm after the load connected to the motor shaft is removed. Enter the 50% of the rated current value when it is difficult to measure H34 - [No Load Motor Current]. Chapter 8.9 (printed 8-14): No-load current: with the load removed, run at 60Hz in V/F control and enter Cur; or enter 40-50% of H33 or the factory default; lower to 30% if torque ripple occurs at high speed.
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. H32 ~ H36 factory default values are set based on OTIS-LG motor.

parameters.name: Motor efficiency
parameters.description: Enter the motor efficiency (see motor nameplate).
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. H32 ~ H36 factory default values are set based on OTIS-LG motor.

parameters.name: Load inertia rate
parameters.description: Select one of the following according to motor inertia. Chapter 8.1 / 8.19 (printed 8-1, 8-26): Load inertia selection (0 less than 10x, 1 about 10x, 2 more than 10x motor inertia); used for DC brake controller gain and energy buffering (a high ratio gives a small frequency change).

parameters.name: Carrier frequency select
parameters.description: This parameter affects the audible sound of the motor, noise emission from the inverter, inverter temp, and leakage current. If the set value is higher, the inverter sound is quieter but the noise from the inverter and leakage current will become greater. Chapter 8.13 (printed 8-19): Higher carrier frequency reduces motor sound but increases inverter heat loss, noise and leakage current.

parameters.name: Control mode select
parameters.description: Chapter 8.6 / 8.9 (printed 8-8, 8-14): 1 Slip compensation: keeps constant speed by compensating motor slip. 3 Sensorless vector: do H41 auto tuning first and enter H30, H32, H33, H34, H42, H44, F14 correctly.

parameters.name: Auto tuning
parameters.description: If this parameter is set to 1, it automatically measures parameters of the H42 and H44. Chapter 8.8 (printed 8-13): Setting 1 and pressing Enter starts auto tuning ("TUn"), measuring H42 and H44; stop with STOP/RST or EST. Execute with the motor stopped; the shaft must not be driven by the load.

parameters.name: Stator resistance (Rs)
parameters.description: This is the value of the motor stator resistance.

parameters.name: Leakage inductance (L sigma)
parameters.description: This is leakage inductance of the stator and rotor of the motor.

parameters.name: Sensorless P gain
parameters.description: P gain for Sensorless control
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: Yes. Set H40 to 3 (Sensorless vector control) to display this parameter.

parameters.name: Sensorless I gain
parameters.description: I gain for Sensorless control
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: Yes. Set H40 to 3 (Sensorless vector control) to display this parameter.

parameters.name: Sensorless torque limit
parameters.description: Limits output torque in sensorless mode.

parameters.name: PWM mode select
parameters.description: If you want to limit an inverter leakage current, select 2 phase PWM mode. It has more noise in comparison to Normal PWM mode.

parameters.name: PID select
parameters.description: Selects whether using PID control or not Chapter 8.7 (printed 8-9, 8-10): Set to 1 to enable PID control; then rEF and Fbk appear in the Drive group. A multi-function input set to 21 switches PID to normal V/F operation.
parameters.evidence_quote: H49 A331 PID select 0~1 Selects whether using PID control or not 0 X 8-10 0 Terminal I input (0 ~ 20 mA) H50

parameters.name: PID F/B select
parameters.description: Chapter 8.7 (printed 8-10): PID feedback source: 0 terminal I (0~20mA), 1 terminal V1 (0~10V).
parameters.setting_conditions: Adjustable during run: No. Set H49 to 1 (PID control) to display this parameter.

parameters.name: P gain for PID

knowledge_items.title: Block diagram 6.1 Frequency setting
knowledge_items.description: Frequency setting block: 1st Reference Frequency, 2nd Reference Frequency (selected by the 2nd Reference Freq. Select multi-function input), Multi-step Frequency (Multi-step Select), JOG Frequency (JOG Select, JOG_FX Select, JOG_RX Select) and the Multi-function inputs that select them. The signal-flow drawing is on page 73 (printed 6-3), which is a graphic with no usable text layer (OCR noise).

knowledge_items.title: Block diagram 6.2 Drive command setting

knowledge_items.title: Block diagram 6.3 Accel/Decel setting and V/F control
knowledge_items.description: Accel/Decel and V/F control block diagram: Reference freq. for Accel/Decel (H70: Max freq. 0 / Delta freq. 1), Accel/Decel time (ACC, dEC, 1st-7th Accel/Decel time I34-I47, selected by multi-function inputs I17-I24 with digital input filter I27), Accel/Decel pattern (F2, F3: Linear 0 / S-curve 1), Stop method select (F4: 0 decel stop, 1 DC brake, 2 free run stop), DC brake (F8-F11), Dwell operation (H7, H8), frequency high/low limit (F25, F26), V/F pattern (F30: 0 Linear, 1 Square, 2 User V/F with F31-F38), Torque boost select (F27: 0 Manual / 1 Automatic; values F28, F29), Output voltage adjustment (F39), Base/start frequency (F22, F23), then PWM.

knowledge_items.title: Frequency setting via keypad (Frq = 0 or 1)
knowledge_items.description: Keypad 1 (Frq=0): set the desired frequency in 0.00 and press the Prog/Ent key to store it. Keypad 2 (Frq=1): in 0.00 the frequency changes when the Up/Down keys are pressed (Up/Down serve as a potentiometer). Values must be less than F21 [Max frequency]. When a remote keypad is connected, the keypad keys on the body are deactivated.

knowledge_items.title: Frequency setting via -10 ~ +10 V input (Frq = 2)
knowledge_items.description: Set Frq to 2. Apply a -10V~+10V signal between V1 and CM. I2~I5 set the input range and corresponding frequency for -10V~0V; I6~I10 for 0~+10V (V1). Example: minimum (-) input voltage -2V with 10Hz and max voltage -8V with 50Hz. The set frequency can be monitored in 0.00.
knowledge_items.evidence_quote: Apply –10V ~ +10V signal between V1 and CM terminal.

knowledge_items.description: Select 3 in Frq. 0-10V is applied from an external controller or from a potentiometer connected to terminals VR, V1 and CM; parameters I6~I10 define filter time constant, min/max voltage and corresponding frequencies (example: 2V = 10Hz, 8V = 50Hz).

Power Braking adjusts the deceleration slope (or accelerates again) when the DC voltage rises because of regeneration; it allows short deceleration without braking resistor but deceleration may take longer than set, and frequent use on repeatedly decelerating loads can overheat the motor. Stall prevention and Power Braking operate only on deceleration and Power Braking has precedence. F61 (voltage limit under Decel) is visible when BIT2 of F59 is set. knowledge_items.title: Kinetic energy buffering (H64 - H67, H37)
knowledge_items.description: On input power failure the DC link voltage drops and a low-voltage trip cuts the output; KEB maintains the DC link voltage by controlling the output frequency during the power failure, lengthening the time from power failure to low-voltage trip. H64 = 0: normal deceleration until low voltage; H64 = 1: the inverter controls output frequency and charges the motor-generated energy into the DC link. H65/H66 select the start and stop levels (manual text says set the stop level higher than the start level based on the low-voltage level); H37 load inertia: a higher inertia ratio gives a smaller frequency change during KEB. Chapter 8 table lists H65 default 130.0 and H66 135.0 whereas the function list (page 58) prints 125.0 and 130.0.

knowledge_items.description: DRAW is a kind of open-loop tension control using the speed difference of a motor running under the main frequency command to keep material tension steady. For 1 and 2 the centre of the analog input range (I6~I15) is the reference (above centre +, below -); for 3 0V is the reference. Example: 30Hz command, F70 = 3, F71 = 10.0 % gives 27Hz (V1 = -10V) to 33Hz (V1 = +10V). CAUTION: set the command frequency in FRQ/FRQ2 and the rest from F70; e.g. FRQ=2 (V1) with F70=1 (V1) does not operate.

knowledge_items.title: LS BUS basic message format (ENQ / ACK / NAK)
knowledge_items.description: Command (request): ENQ (1 byte), Drive No (2 bytes), CMD (1 byte), Data (n bytes), SUM (2 bytes), EOT (1 byte). Normal response: ACK, Drive No, CMD, Data (n x 4 bytes), SUM, EOT. Negative response: NAK, Drive No, CMD, Error code (2 bytes), SUM (2 bytes), EOT. Drive number is 2-byte ASCII-HEX. Data is ASCII-HEX (e.g. data value 3000 decimal = "0BB8" = 30h 42h 42h 38h).

knowledge_items.title: LS BUS CMD characters, buffers and SUM calculation
knowledge_items.description: CMD (capital letter): R = 52h Read, W = 57h Write, X = 58h Request for monitoring, Y = 59h Action for monitoring. Error code: ASCII 20h~7Fh. Receive/send buffer size: receive 39 bytes, send 44 bytes; monitor register buffer 8 words. SUM = ASCII-HEX of the lower 8 bits of (Drive No + CMD + DATA); control characters ENQ/ACK/NAK are excluded. Example: read one address from "3000": ENQ 05h, "01", "R", "3000", "1", SUM "A7", EOT 04h (SUM = 30h+31h+52h+33h+30h+30h+30h+31h = 1A7h).

knowledge_items.title: Parameter setting procedure (example: ACC time)
knowledge_items.description: Select the code (Up key), press Ent to display the value, use Left/Up to change the digits, press Ent (the value blinks) and Ent again to store it. Pressing Left/Right/Up/Down while the value is blinking cancels the change; pressing Enter in that status enters the value into memory.

knowledge_items.title: Frequency setting procedure (example: 30.05 Hz)
knowledge_items.description: In "0.00" press Ent, set the digits with Up/Left keys, press Ent (30.05 blinks), press Ent to enter into memory. SV-iG5A display can be extended to 5 digits using left/right keys. Parameter setting is disabled when pressing other than Enter Key in step 7.

knowledge_items.title: Changing a parameter value via code jump (example: F28 from 2 to 5)

knowledge_items.title: Monitoring output current in Drive group

knowledge_items.title: Fault display on the keypad
knowledge_items.description: When a fault occurs, the fault message is displayed; press Enter or UP/Down to see the run frequency at the time of fault, then the output current, then the operating status (e.g. fault during acceleration). knowledge_items.title: Parameter initialize procedure (H93)

knowledge_items.title: Low voltage
knowledge_items.description: The inverter turns off its output if the DC voltage is below 180V because insufficient torque or overheating of the motor can occur when the input voltage of the inverter drops.
knowledge_items.cause: Line voltage is low; Load larger than line capacity is connected to line (ex: welding machine, motor with high starting current connected to the commercial line); Faulty magnetic switch at the input side of the inverter.
knowledge_items.remedy: Check whether line voltage is below its rating; Check the incoming AC line; Adjust the line capacity corresponding to the load; Change a magnetic switch.

knowledge_items.remedy: Reduce load weight and operating duty; Change inverter with higher capacity; Adjust ETH level to an appropriate level; Select correct inverter capacity; Install a cooling fan with a separate power supply.

knowledge_items.title: EMC filter recommended installation instructions
knowledge_items.description: 1) Check the filter rating label (current, voltage, part number). 2) Fit the filter as close as possible to the incoming mains supply, usually directly after the enclosure's circuit breaker or supply switch. 3) Prepare the back panel mounting area; remove paint etc. from mounting holes and face for best earthing. 4) Mount the filter securely. 5) Connect mains to the filter terminals marked LINE, earth cables to the earth stud; connect filter terminals marked LOAD to the inverter mains input with short lengths of appropriate gauge cable. 6) Connect the motor and fit the ferrite core (output chokes) as close to the inverter as possible; use armoured or screened cable with the 3 phase conductors only threaded twice through the ferrite core; earth conductor securely earthed at both ends; screen connected to enclosure body via an earthed cable gland. 7) Connect control cables as instructed. All lead lengths must be kept as short as possible and incoming mains and outgoing motor cables kept well separated.

notes: Code notation: parameter codes are normalized by removing the space the manual prints inside single-digit codes ("F 0" -> "F0", "H 1" -> "H1", "I 0" -> "I0"); two-digit codes (F10, H33, I54 ...) are as printed (I82-I87 are printed as "182".."187" in the text layer and are read as I82-I87). DRV group codes are the LED mnemonics (0.00, ACC, dEC, drv, Frq, St1-St3, CUr, rPM, dCL, vOL, nOn, drC, drv2, Frq2, rEF, Fbk). Footnote markers ("1)", "2)") printed next to codes were removed; the footnote text is stored in setting_conditions.

Parameter "Address for communication" values (hex, e.g. A100, A200, A300, A400) are stored ONLY in modbus_registers (name "<name> (<code>)"), not in the parameter records. The function list does not state read/write access or function codes for them (access null, function_codes null). The drv address is printed as A103 in this version. H71 and H87 are both printed with address A347 on pages 59 and 60 (H87 is probably a typo for A357); both are recorded as printed.

RS-485 register lists (chapter 11, pages 156-161): common area 0x0000-0x001F, read/write address registers 0x0100-0x010F, extended common area 0x0300-0x031A (monitoring), 0x0320-0x0389 (control), 0x03E2/0x03E5 (memory control) are stored in modbus_registers. Addresses 0x320 and 0x321 are printed without the leading zero and normalized to 0x0320/0x0321. The common-area table is a merged-cell layout: the bit text of 0x0005/0x0006 (frequency reference / run command) and of 0x0330-0x0334 (latch type trip information, warning) is vertically merged in the text layer, so the bit allotment was assigned by reading the layout and may be mis-assigned between neighbouring rows. 0x0000/0x0001 inverter model/capacity codes are printed in a broken layout (0x0001 value list starts with FFFF : 0.4kW, then 0000 : 0.75kW, 0002 ... 000B). The common-area table prints R/W '-' for 0x000E. Function codes are not stated per register; the Modbus-RTU function codes (0x03, 0x04, 0x06, 0x10) and LS BUS commands (R, W, X, Y) are recorded in communication knowledge items.

Function list text layer is a flattened table; values were transcribed by hand and re-checked against the new page text (page range 45-69). Columns shared by several rows (merged cells: range/description/default of F3, dEC, St2-St3, F32-F38, H12-H16, H81-H90, I3-I47 and the option lists of I17-I24 and I54/I55, adj-during-run of I66-I81) are repeated for each row where the layout makes the assignment clear. F3 default 0 and adj X are taken from the merged cell of F2/F3. Descriptions for rows whose description cell is merged were left null or reference the shared text. F61 has no initial value or adj. cell printed (null). Parameter H59 and I88, which exist in an older version of the manual, are NOT in this manual and are not extracted.

Adjustable-during-run column: printed O / X; some cells appear as the digit "0" in the text layer (F40, F50-F58, F71, rEF). They are read as O (Yes) and flagged in setting_conditions. The I65 initial value is printed as the letter "O" (read as 0). H22 has its bit table split over pages 54-55 (adj O on page 54).

Inconsistencies inside the manual (recorded as printed, not corrected): H72 range 0~15 in the function list but options 0-17 listed there and in 9.1; H65/H66 defaults 125.0/130.0 (function list) vs 130.0/135.0 (section 8.19); H48 range 0~1 (function list) vs 0~2 (8.21); H33/H34 ranges in chapter 8 tables (0.5~50, 0.1~20) differ from the function list (0.5~150, 0.1~50); F26 min 0.1 (function list) vs 0 (chapter 7); section 7.1 refers to "Chapter 13. RS485 communication" (it is chapter 11); 11.1 says up to 31 drives while 11.2 says max 16.

Bit tables with check marks (F59 stall prevention, H22 speed search, I56 fault relay output, I57 output terminal select on keypad communication error, multi-step / Multi-Accel/Decel selection tables) lost their check-mark glyphs in the text layer (they appear as the digit 3 or 9, or are missing); the bit meanings are recorded from the headings and examples.

OCR / no-text pages: page 1 (cover, OCR), page 13 (nearly empty: "Notes:" and printed page 1-4), page 73 and 74 (block diagrams 6.1/6.2, OCR noise), page 76 (empty Notes page), page 181 (filter dimension drawings, OCR garbage). Page 70 has no text (empty). Printed page for page 13 is taken from its last line (1-4); other pages use the first line. No quotes were taken from OCR pages except page 181 heading line "FS SERIES (output chokes)".

Page 123 repeats the content of page 121 (duplicate page in the PDF, printed 8-23); only page 121 is cited for chapter 8.16. Graphics not extracted as text: dimension drawings (pp16-19), terminal/wiring figures (pp20-26), keypad LED glyph shapes (p31), keypad fault-code images (pp163-167; fault keypad codes are null except EEP, HWT, Err, COM, NTC printed as text on page 167), control block diagrams (pp72-75), PID block diagrams (pp109-110), timing diagrams in chapters 7-10, remote keypad/conduit kit installation drawings.

Fault tables (pages 163-167): the keypad display column is made of images, so fault codes are null except where printed as text. Fault titles are the manual protective-function names; cause/remedy come from the Fault remedy table (pages 165-166); some entries (Self-diagnostic malfunction, Input phase loss, Instant cut off) have no cause/remedy row in the manual. Self-diagnostic result codes (UPHF ... WPOF) on page 120 are recorded as fault items.

Merged-cell tables (power terminal wire size/torque p22, MCCB p28, fuse/reactor p29, RFI filters p180, ratings p169-170) are stored with details transcribed as printed; some model-to-value assignments follow the visual merge. The FF/FE filter tables on page 180 are stored as printed row lines. The control block diagrams of chapter 6 are described from their text labels only.

Importance tiers were assigned from the parameter function per the README rubric; common_function mappings are only given where the manual documents the same function (Exact Equivalent) or a close one (Functionally Similar). Descriptions of many parameters were extended with the explanation from chapters 7-10 (stated as 'Chapter N.N: ...' inside the description); the evidence quote and page of those parameters remain the function-list row.
